classification.classification_note: The saved AddressSanitizer report is a zero-PC SEGV / null-deref READ. Source reconstruction shows the underlying defect is a use-before-initialization of the global `notes` obstack control block in the vulnerable `fuzz_as` harness, whose concrete sink is a NULL allocator-function-pointer call in `call_chunkfun()`.

bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 4-byte file `.mac` (`2e 6d 61 63`), which the vulnerable `fuzz_as.c` harness writes to `/tmp/libfuzzer-<pid>.s`. The saved AddressSanitizer trace shows that the crash happens before any assembly bytes are lexed or assembled. Instead of entering the real GAS `main()` initialization sequence, the harness manually calls `symbol_begin(); frag_init(); subsegs_begin(); read_begin();` but omits the earlier `obstack_begin(&notes, chunksize)` that `gas/as.c:1288` executes before `read_begin()`. When `read_begin()` runs, `pobegin()` creates the pseudo-op hash table with `str_htab_create()`, which hard-wires `notes_calloc` as the table allocator. `htab_create_typed_alloc()` immediately invokes that allocator to allocate the `struct htab` header. `notes_calloc()` delegates to `notes_alloc()`, and `notes_alloc()` calls `obstack_alloc(&notes, size)` on the never-begun global `notes` obstack. In `libiberty/obstack.c`, `call_chunkfun()` then dispatches through `notes.chunkfun.plain == NULL`, so control jumps to `pc=0x0` and AddressSanitizer reports the saved null-dereference READ. The staged patch only adds `free(matching)` in `ada_addr2line.h` and does not address this `fuzz_as` initialization-order bug.

source.description: First non-harness project-side use of the invalid startup state. `pobegin()` begins constructing the pseudo-op hash table and, through `str_htab_create()`, selects the `notes`-backed allocator path before any assembly bytes are lexed.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness is the 4-byte file `2e 6d 61 63` (`.mac`), which `fuzz_as.c` writes to `/tmp/libfuzzer-<pid>.s` and passes as `fakeArgv[1]`. The saved stack shows the crash happens during `read_begin()` before `input_scrub_begin()` or `perform_an_assembly_pass()` read that file, so the only verified input-side fact is that this temp assembly path exists when `pobegin()` runs; no byte-dependent project parse occurs before the fault.
source.note: Source. This is the first project statement on the witnessed path that turns the harness's missing `notes` initialization into a concrete `notes_calloc` allocation request for pseudo-op state.

sink.description: Source-grounded null-function-pointer sink. `call_chunkfun()` dispatches through the obstack's plain chunk allocator hook, but on the never-begun `notes` obstack that hook is still NULL.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports only `pc=0x0`, `<unknown module>`, and a READ from address `0x0`. This line is the concrete zero-page call target consistent with the saved frames `notes_alloc -> notes_calloc -> htab_create_typed_alloc -> htab_create_alloc -> str_htab_create -> pobegin -> read_begin`.

root_cause.description: The harness invokes `read_begin()` without first executing the required `obstack_begin(&notes, chunksize)` that real `gas/as.c:main()` performs before the same startup sequence. That missing initialization leaves the global `notes` obstack with NULL allocator hooks.
root_cause.note: In `gas/as.c`, line 1288 runs `obstack_begin (&notes, chunksize)` before the later `symbol_begin (); frag_init (); subsegs_begin (); read_begin ();` block at lines 1335-1338. The vulnerable harness copies only the latter block, so `read_begin()` runs with `notes.chunkfun.plain == NULL`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the never-begun global `notes` obstack. When the harness reaches `read_begin()` without the earlier `obstack_begin(&notes, chunksize)`, the obstack control fields remain in their zero-initialized state and the later allocator call path uses `notes.chunkfun.plain == NULL`.

parser_admitted.description: The harness reaches GAS reader initialization and enters `pobegin()` for the staged temp `.s` file. The crash happens immediately in pseudo-op-table setup, before `input_scrub_begin()` or `perform_an_assembly_pass()` can lex any assembly text.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness writes the 4-byte witness `.mac` to a temp `.s` file and manually runs part of GAS startup, but omits `obstack_begin(&notes, chunksize)` before calling `read_begin()`.
`read_begin()` enters `pobegin()`, which starts building the pseudo-op hash table and routes allocation through `str_htab_create()`.
`str_htab_create()` binds `notes_calloc` as the hash-table allocator and calls into libiberty hashtab creation.
Hash-table creation immediately invokes that allocator to allocate the `struct htab` header.
`notes_calloc()` delegates to `notes_alloc()`, which calls `obstack_alloc(&notes, size)` even though the global `notes` obstack was never begun.
`call_chunkfun()` dispatches through `notes.chunkfun.plain == NULL`, explaining the saved zero-PC null-dereference READ.

fine_trace.note: Root cause. The harness enters GAS reader initialization without the earlier `obstack_begin (&notes, chunksize)` that real `gas/as.c:main()` executes before `read_begin()`. The global `notes` obstack is therefore still in its zero-initialized state with NULL chunk allocator hooks.

Source. `pobegin()` starts pseudo-op table creation before any assembly bytes are lexed. On this path `str_htab_create()` is the first project-side use of the unbegun `notes` state, because it routes allocation through `notes_calloc`.

fine_trace.code:
return htab_create_alloc (16, hash_string_tuple, eq_string_tuple,
                            NULL, notes_calloc, NULL);
fine_trace.note: The helper binds `notes_calloc` as the allocator for this hash table and supplies no free function. Both the table header and the entries array will therefore come from the `notes` obstack path.

fine_trace.code:
return htab_create_typed_alloc (size, hash_f, eq_f, del_f, alloc_f, alloc_f,
                                  free_f);
fine_trace.note: The wrapper forwards that same `notes_calloc` function as both `alloc_tab_f` and `alloc_f`, so the very first `struct htab` allocation also uses the `notes` obstack path.

Hash-table construction immediately invokes `notes_calloc(1, sizeof(struct htab))` to allocate the table header. Execution never reaches the later `result->entries` allocation because this first allocator call already faults.

For this first table-header request, `n = 1` and `size = sizeof (struct htab)`, so the overflow check is false, `amt` becomes the header size, and `notes_calloc()` delegates the actual allocation to `notes_alloc(amt)`.

`notes_alloc()` uses the global `notes` obstack as its storage backend. Because step 1 never executed `obstack_begin (&notes, chunksize)`, this call reaches the obstack machinery while `notes.chunkfun.plain` is still NULL.

Sink. `call_chunkfun()` selects the plain allocator hook and calls through `h->chunkfun.plain`; on the zero-initialized but never-begun `notes` obstack that function pointer is NULL, so control transfers to `pc=0x0` and AddressSanitizer reports the saved null-dereference READ.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` only adds `free (matching)` in `ada_addr2line.h`. It does not touch `fuzz_as.c`, `gas/read.c`, `gas/symbols.c`, `gas/hash.h`, `libiberty/hashtab.c`, `libiberty/obstack.c`, or the missing `obstack_begin(&notes, chunksize)` precondition behind this crash.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, and the exact staged vulnerable source snapshot; `patch.diff` is unrelated to the witnessed `fuzz_as` null-deref.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Partially. AddressSanitizer frame 0 is only `pc=0x0` / `<unknown module>`, but the saved project frames `notes_alloc -> notes_calloc -> htab_create_typed_alloc -> htab_create_alloc -> str_htab_create -> pobegin -> read_begin` close to fine-trace step 8, the concrete NULL `chunkfun.plain` call that explains a zero-page READ on this path.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The reconstructed chain follows the exact saved stack, and the staged source shows that `notes_alloc` can only reach a zero-PC fault here if `call_chunkfun()` dispatches through an uninitialized `notes.chunkfun.plain`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Not through parsed assembly bytes. The staged witness only drives the vulnerable harness far enough to call `read_begin()` on the temp `.s` file; the crash happens before project code lexes the file contents. The closed source-grounded chain is instead the invalid startup-state flow from the harness's missing `obstack_begin(&notes, chunksize)` to the NULL allocator-function-pointer call at the sink.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash with `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_48997 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reported `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / null-deref READ with stack `notes_alloc -> notes_calloc -> htab_create_typed_alloc -> htab_create_alloc -> str_htab_create -> pobegin -> read_begin`.

format.name: 4-byte `fuzz_as` temp assembly file witness
format.contract: The exact staged witness is the 4-byte file `.mac` (`2e 6d 61 63`, sha256 `b3c1895fcdc56b4a941b4b5a0d6824524a5d3c48b4b5d7684fcf2f659efb6b88`). `fuzz_as.c` writes those bytes to `/tmp/libfuzzer-<pid>.s`, but the saved crash occurs during `read_begin()` before `input_scrub_begin()` or `perform_an_assembly_pass()` read that file. The staged artifacts therefore justify only this exact witness and the startup-order precondition it exercises; they do not prove any broader assembly-syntax requirement or any claim that arbitrary byte strings would reproduce the fault.

evidence_limitations: The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated to the witnessed `fuzz_as` crash and was not used as the causal oracle.

The saved failure occurs before assembler input bytes are lexed, so Stage 02 cannot attribute the bug to any parsed assembly directive or broader byte-dependent input class beyond the exact 4-byte witness.
